RENTOMOJO | Q1 FY27 RESULT

Financial Performance
- Revenue: ₹126.3 Cr | +51.4% YoY | +15.3% QoQ
- EBITDA: ₹51.5 Cr | +55.8% YoY | +14.4% QoQ
- EBITDA Margin: 40.8% vs 39.6% YoY
- PAT: ₹10.6 Cr | -9.2% YoY | -53.4% QoQ
- EPS: ₹34.47 | Flat YoY & QoQ

Key Positives
- Revenue growth remained strong at 51.4% YoY.
- EBITDA growth outpaced revenue growth.
- EBITDA margin improved 1.2pp YoY.
- Operating profitability remained strong.

Key Watch
- PAT declined despite strong EBITDA growth.
- Other income fell 30.6% YoY.
- Other income declined sharply to ₹0.77 Cr.
- PAT was impacted by lower other income.

Market Data
- CMP: ₹510.80 | -2.83%
- Market Cap: ₹5,318 Cr

KEY TAKEAWAY
Rentomojo delivered strong operating growth with 51% revenue and 56% EBITDA growth YoY. However, PAT declined 9% YoY, mainly reflecting the sharp fall in other income.

BLUE WATER LOGISTICS: INCORPORATES WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY IN VIETNAM

• Incorporated Blue Water Logistics Vietnam Company Limited as a 100% wholly owned subsidiary.
• Subsidiary will undertake freight forwarding, warehousing/storage and other logistics activities in Vietnam.
• Company will invest around VND 2.61 billion (~US$100,000) as capital.
• Subsidiary was incorporated on September 29, 2026; registration certificate received on October 5.
Impact: Positive — Vietnam entry expands Blue Water Logistics’ international footprint and provides a platform to grow cross-border logistics business.

TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED : VESSEL SALE TRANSACTION COMPLETED

• The sale of the company's vessel, M.V. SSL Sabarimalai, to Avana Logistek Limited has been successfully completed on 05th October 2026.
• The transaction follows the execution of the Protocol of Delivery and Acceptance between the buyer and seller.
• The vessel was delivered at Vishakhapatnam, India.
Impact: Neutral (Routine transaction of vessel sale)

IREDA : SIGNS PERFORMANCE MOU WITH MNRE FOR FY 2026-27

ETHOS LIMITED : CHANGE IN SENIOR MANAGEMENT

• Mr. Rajesh Pandey has resigned as National Sales Head of the Company.
• His resignation is effective from the close of business hours on October 05, 2026.
• The reason for resignation is to pursue career opportunities outside the company.
• The company is in the process of identifying a suitable successor.
Impact: Neutral (Resignation of a senior management official, with no immediate financial implications stated.)

HLE GLASCOAT: RESTRUCTURING OF STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY SHARES

• Thaletec GmbH, a wholly owned subsidiary, has transferred 100% shareholding in HLE Surface Technologies GmbH (step-down subsidiary) to HLE International S.à.r.l. (wholly owned subsidiary).
• The transaction is effective October 5, 2026.
• The restructuring is intended to rationalize and simplify the overall group structure.
• Details as per SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 are enclosed as Annexure-A.
Impact: Neutral (Internal corporate restructuring for simplification)

SOLEX ENERGY : WINS RS 13.16 CR ORDER

• Solex Energy Limited secured a work order from a domestic entity.
• The order is for the supply of TopCon Bifacial G2G 620Wp Solar PV Modules.
• The total order value is ₹13.16 Crores, inclusive of applicable taxes.
• The work is scheduled to be executed till November, 2026.
Impact: Positive (Order win adds to revenue pipeline)

KOTHARI SUGARS AND CHEMICALS : NCLT CHENNAI ALLOWS SCHEME OF AMALGAMATION

• NCLT Chennai allowed the application and directed KSCL & KPL to convene meetings of shareholders and unsecured creditors on Nov 13, 2026.
• Meetings are to consider and approve the scheme of amalgamation between KSCL & KPL.
• Indian Bank, secured creditor, provided consent, dispensing with meeting of secured creditors.
• Scheme remains subject to statutory and regulatory approvals.
Impact: Positive (Scheme of amalgamation progressing with NCLT approval for shareholder and creditor meetings.)

AWL AGRI BUSINESS : Q2 BIZ

• AWL reported 12% YoY volume growth and 24% YoY revenue growth in Q2 FY27.
• Food & FMCG segment revenue grew 33% YoY, crossing ₹2,000 crore for the first time.
• Edible Oil business recorded 3% YoY volume growth.
• Industry Essentials recorded 25% YoY volume growth.
• Alternate Channels (E-Commerce, Quick Commerce, Modern Trade) delivered double-digit growth.
• Branded Exports saw 59% YoY volume growth.
• Impact: Board approval pending for detailed financial results.

JAPAN COMPANIES CUT CHINA EXPOSURE, INDIA EMERGES AS ALTERNATIVE HUB

• Japanese companies operating in China fell to 10,118 in June 2026, down 22% in two years and nearly 30% from the 2012 peak.
• Between 2024–2026, around 4,137 Japanese companies exited/disappeared from China, while only 1,221 new entrants were added.
• Key concerns include intense Chinese competition, overcapacity, rare-earth restrictions and geopolitical tensions.
• India is increasingly being considered for manufacturing and investment diversification, supported by its large domestic market.
Impact: Positive for India — relocation and diversification by Japanese companies could accelerate FDI, manufacturing capacity and supply-chain investments.

ZYDUS LIFESCIENCES : LAUNCHES FIRST GENERIC OF ADEMPAS IN US

• Zydus and MSN announced the launch of Riociguat Tablets (0.5 mg to 2.5 mg) in the United States.
• This is the first generic version of Adempas® (riociguat) to be launched in the U.S. market.
• The product was developed and is manufactured by MSN.
• Riociguat is indicated for adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH).
• The global sales of Adempas® were approximately EUR 745 million (approx. USD 850 million) in 2025.
Impact: Positive (First generic launch expands access to PAH/CTEPH treatment in the US)

ACME SOLAR HOLDINGS LIMITED : EXPANSION OF COMMISSIONED SOLAR CAPACITY

• ACME Renewtech Private Limited, a subsidiary, commissioned an additional 66.68 MW of solar capacity at Village- Kelan, Tehsil-Chhatargarh, District-Bikaner, Rajasthan.
• The Commercial Operation Date (COD) for this capacity is October 07, 2026.
• With this addition, ACME Renewtech Private Limited has achieved a commissioned solar capacity of 133.36 MW out of the total 300 MW for the Hybrid Power Project.
• The Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) for this project has been signed with NTPC Limited.
Impact: Positive (Expansion of commissioned solar capacity contributing to the overall hybrid power project.)

MARICO LIMITED: ACQUIRES 84.09% STAKE IN SATIYA NUTRACEUTICALS

• Marico Limited acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited, increasing its aggregate stake to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
• The current tranche of acquisition was for a consideration of ₹1,012.03 crore.
• The aggregate consideration for 84.09% stake stands at ₹1,392.07 crore.
• The remaining 14.09% stake is to be acquired in July 2027 for an aggregate consideration of up to ₹592 crore plus additional consideration based on milestones.
• Satiya Nutraceuticals owns the brand 'The Plant Fix – Plix', a plant-based nutrition and personal care brand.
• For FY23-24, Satiya Nutraceuticals reported a consolidated turnover of ₹155.32 crore.
Impact: Positive (Increases Marico's stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, expanding its presence in the health and wellness segment.)

• Upon completion of the acquisition, the Acquirers will acquire control of the Target Company.

ADANI ENT ; AIRLINES CHALLENGE MUMBAI T1 REDEVELOPMENT PLAN : REPORT

• Airlines dispute Adani Airports’ 33% capacity reduction assessment.
• Seek clarity on whether 33% refers to flights, slots, passengers or terminal capacity.
• Demand consultation records and capacity-utilisation data before any changes.
• Oppose unilateral slot cuts, cancellations or relocation until consultations are completed.
Impact: Neutral to Negative — airline resistance may delay smooth execution of the T1 redevelopment plan.

• Secured creditor Indian Bank has consented, and the NCLT dispensed with the meeting of secured creditors.

JSW ENERGY LTD : INSTALLED CAPACITY REACHES 15.1 GW

• Company added 1,694 MW of installed capacity since April 2026, including ~1.4 GW of renewable capacity.
• Total installed capacity increased to 15,147 MW.
• The capacity added includes 593 MW of solar, 108 MW of wind, 542 MW of hybrid and 150 MW of hydro projects, along with 300 MW of inorganic thermal capacity.
• Renewable energy now constitutes ~61% (9,189 MW) of the operational portfolio.
• JSW Energy has a total locked-in generation capacity of 32.4 GW and energy storage capacity of 29.6 GWh.
• Company targets 30 GW of generation capacity and 40 GWh of energy storage by 2030.
Impact: Positive (Capacity expansion aligns with long-term growth strategy and renewable energy targets.)

TAMILNAD MERCANTILE BANK : INDIA RATINGS ASSIGNS 'IND AA-'; OUTLOOK STABLE

• Issuer rating of "IND AA-" with a "Stable" outlook assigned by India Ratings.
• Reflects improved profitability, prudent provisioning, and adequate capitalization.
• Strengths: stable funding franchise, improving asset quality, healthy capital buffers.
• Weaknesses: modest loan book size, geographic concentration, shareholding overhang.
• Liquidity position is adequate.
Impact: Rating assignment could influence investor sentiment and borrowing costs.

WINDSOR MACHINES LIMITED : APPOINTS MOHAN RAMACHANDRAN AS ADDITIONAL DIRECTOR

• Mohan Ramachandran appointed as Additional Director (Executive, Non-independent) designated as Whole-time Director and Chief Executive Officer.
• Appointment effective from October 05, 2026 for a period of three years, up to October 04, 2029.
• Ramachandran has over 32 years of experience in automotive and industrial manufacturing.
• He is not related to any director of the Company and is not debarred from holding office by any order of SEBI or other authority.

VSF PROJECTS LIMITED : GRANT OF LETTER OF APPROVAL FOR UNIT BY HINA TEXTILE MILLS PRIVATE LIMITED

• Office of the Development Commissioner, Visakhapatnam SEZ, issued Letter of Approval (Form-G) dated October 05, 2026
• Approval permits Hina Textile Mills Private Limited to set up a unit in the FTWZ of VSF Projects Limited
• Authorised operations include bonded warehousing, storage, packing/repacking/labelling of specified items like cashew nuts, coconut, cotton, fabrics, and agricultural sprayers.
• Company will lease warehouse space and earn revenues from ICD containers used by Hina Textile Mills
• Letter of Approval is valid from October 05, 2026, to October 04, 2027, for project implementation and commencement of operations.
• Upon commencement, approval is valid for five years.
Impact: Positive (Enhances FTWZ utilization and revenue streams through new unit setup)

BROACH LIFECARE HOSPITAL LIMITED : GENERAL ANNOUNCEMENT – STRATEGIC INSTITUTIONAL EMPANELMENT, EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE SERVICES AND PROGRESS TOWARDS NABH ACCREDITATION

• Hospital has received its Income Tax Exemption Certificate under Form 17/2 and has been empaneled with ONGC to provide cashless healthcare services.
• Empanelment with other Government PSUs, including GACL and GNFC, is currently underway.
• Hospital has been empaneled with ESIC to provide healthcare services to eligible beneficiaries.
• Hospital has expanded its PMJAY service capabilities by adding Cardiothoracic Surgery, Urology, and a 5-bed Dialysis Unit.
• Hospital has successfully completed its Full NABH Accreditation Inspection and is currently awaiting the Accreditation Committee's decision.
Impact: Positive (Strategic initiatives to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and expand service capabilities in the Bharuch region)

AMBER ENTERPRISES: ₹38.28 CRORE LOSS ESTIMATED FROM ILJIN FACTORY FIRE; INSURER PAYS ₹10 CRORE

• Fire occurred on August 4, 2026 at material subsidiary ILJIN Electronics (India) facility in Greater Noida.
• Management has estimated the loss at approximately ₹38.28 crore plus applicable GST.
• Company has lodged an insurance claim for the entire estimated loss, along with applicable GST.
• Insurer has already released an on-account payment of ₹10 crore against the claim.
• Detailed assessment of the remaining insurance claim is underway; balance payment will be released after completion of assessment.
• Company expects to recover a majority of the losses and is working on restoration and normalisation of the affected facility.
Impact: Neutral to Positive — the fire caused a material loss, but insurance coverage and the ₹10 crore initial payout significantly reduce the potential financial impact.

NELCAST: TO SET UP ₹75 CRORE MACHINING DIVISION IN ANDHRA PRADESH

• Board approved setting up a new Machining Division at Gudur, Andhra Pradesh.
• Estimated investment of approximately ₹75 crore.
• Project will be funded through a combination of internal accruals and borrowings.
• New facility will provide in-house machining and assembly capabilities for the company’s cast components.
• Expansion will enable Nelcast to offer integrated casting + machining + assembly solutions to customers.
• Project is aimed at increasing value addition, expanding the product portfolio and strengthening manufacturing capabilities.
Impact: Positive — ₹75 crore capex toward downstream machining can improve value addition, customer wallet share and the mix of higher-value products.

JUNIPER HOTELS: BINDING MOU SIGNED FOR HOTEL ACQUISITION WORTH OVER RS 248 CR

• The transaction is not a related party transaction and is done at arm's length.
• Definitive documents are expected to be executed shortly.
Impact: Positive (Acquisition of a strategic hotel property to expand Juniper's portfolio)

STEAMHOUSE INDIA | Q1 FY27 RECORD PERFORMANCE + GREEN ENERGY EXPANSION

Q1 FY27 Financial Performance
- Steam sold reached 305,816 tons.
- Steam volume grew 16.7% YoY.
- Steam volume increased 11.52% QoQ.
- Revenue stood at ₹128.62 Cr.
- Revenue grew 13.35% YoY.
- EBITDA reached ₹30.93 Cr.
- EBITDA grew 60.08% YoY.
- EBITDA margin improved to 24.05%.
- PAT reached ₹18.34 Cr.
- PAT grew 80.25% YoY.

Steam Business
- Steam sales revenue reached ₹123.37 Cr.
- Steam sales grew 46.07% YoY.
- Coal sales revenue was nil in Q1 FY27.
- Q1 FY26 coal sales were ₹28.26 Cr.
- Higher steam sales offset the coal revenue decline.

EBITDA Improvement
- EBITDA per ton increased 37.17%.
- EBITDA per ton reached ₹1,011.
- Earlier EBITDA per ton was ₹737.
- Higher utilization improved operating leverage.
- Waste-to-energy boilers supported efficiency.
- Clean EBITDA rose 65.43% YoY.
- Clean EBITDA reached ₹29.22 Cr.
- Clean EBITDA reflects underlying operating performance.

Major EPC Order
- Company received a ₹311 Cr EPC mandate.
- Project involves a 300 TPH community boiler.
- Project is located at Bulk Drug Park, Una.
- Long-term O&M is included.
- O&M can provide recurring revenue potential.

Green Energy Expansion
- Company is expanding its green-energy portfolio.
- 3.04 MW AC solar project planned.
- Project is ground-mounted at Ankleshwar.
- Green boiler capacity is expanding significantly.
- Capacity targets 105 TPH in FY27.
- FY26 capacity stood at 15 TPH.
- This represents ~7x capacity expansion.

New Growth Opportunities
- EOI submitted for a 400 TPD project.
- Proposed project is Waste-to-Steam based.
- Surat Municipal Corporation is the project authority.
- Community boiler footprint remains a growth focus.
- Company plans participation in upcoming tenders.

Nitrogen Business
- Nitrogen business expansion continues.
- Pipeline infrastructure supports the expansion.
- Management plans further geographic expansion.
- New projects will support business diversification.

Management Commentary
- Q1 FY27 was described as a landmark quarter.
- Management highlighted resilient operational performance.
- Steam volumes remained strong despite macro challenges.
- Higher coal costs were managed through pass-through.
- Fuel-cost increases can be passed to customers.
- Government policies support community boiler opportunities.
- Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 may support infrastructure.
- Management plans further tender participation.

Strategic Roadmap
- Company is developing a diversified fuel mix.
- Waste-to-energy remains a key growth area.
- Decarbonization remains a strategic focus.
- Sustainable energy solutions are being prioritized.
- Technology and innovation remain key priorities.
- Company targets 30–35% EBITDA CAGR over three years.

KEY TAKEAWAY
Steamhouse India delivered strong Q1 FY27 growth, led by higher steam volumes, operating leverage and waste-to-energy utilization. The ₹311 Cr EPC order, 7x green-boiler expansion, solar project and waste-to-steam opportunities provide multiple growth avenues, while management targets 30–35% EBITDA CAGR over the next three years.

🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞
Date: 05 OCTOBER 2026
Telegram: [https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews]

📍 ORDER WIN

BONDADA ENGINEERING: Secures ₹911.25 Cr financing sanction from SBI for a 225 MW solar IPP project backed by a 25-year PPA with MSEDCL.

MARINE ELECTRICALS: Secures multiple orders worth ₹393.52 Cr across data centres, shipbuilding and port infrastructure, with execution timelines of 4–28 months.

STEAMHOUSE INDIA: Wins ₹311 Cr EPC mandate for a community boiler project at Una and is strengthening its green-energy portfolio with a 3.04 MW AC solar project.

SIMPLEX INFRASTRUCTURES: Wins ₹255.52 Cr oil drilling services contract from Oil India, taking FY27 order inflows to approximately ₹920 Cr so far.

AURIONPRO: Wins ₹150 Cr order from a global hyperscaler for an AI-ready data centre in Navi Mumbai, taking projects from the client to nearly ₹300 Cr in under a year.

LASER POWER & INFRA: Secures ₹72.76 Cr contracts from Power Grid for HTLS conductor supply and reconductoring of two 132 kV transmission lines.

A B INFRABUILD: Wins ₹48.09 Cr EPC order from the Government of Chhattisgarh for construction of two grade separators on NH-53, with an 18-month execution period.

DANISH POWER: Receives ₹35 Cr order for design, manufacture and supply of 20 MVA PCS transformers for BESS applications, with execution in 6–8 months.

GUJARAT INJECT: Secures ₹4.86 Cr domestic order for supply of 3,600 solar PV modules, scheduled for execution in October 2026.

ITCONS E-SOLUTIONS: Wins ₹1.93 Cr EPFO contract to provide 48 resources for one year from October 3, 2026.

UAEJTL INDUSTRIES: Secures approximately 5,000 MT export order from Canada for Black Welded Hollow Sections.

📍 ACQUISITION

SAI PARENTERALS: Acquires 60% stake in Prathyak Laboratories for ₹15 Cr, adding an R&D centre with 28 scientists and a pipeline of 150 SKUs across 86 molecules.

VARDHMAN TEXTILES: To acquire minimum 26% stake in Serentica Renewables India 32 for ₹41.85 Cr to develop captive wind and solar power projects.

MAITHAN ALLOYS: Acquires 0.17% stake in HFCL for ₹60.09 Cr through the stock exchange as a long-term investment.

SANGAM (INDIA): Acquires 0.97% stake in CGE II Hybrid Energy for ₹4.76 Cr to support up to 5 MW of captive renewable power consumption.

THIRUMALAI CHEMICALS: Acquires an additional 3.25% stake in Ultramarine & Pigments through the open market, taking its holding to 6.13%.

AJEL: Proposes to acquire Zineeverse Motion Pictures' digital streaming, software development and content business through a share swap, subject to due diligence and definitive agreements.

VACRO ENTERPRISES: Acquires 24.76% stake in Hemo Organic through preferential allotment for ₹1.70 Cr.

QMIN REALITIES: Acquires 24.76% stake in Hemo Organic through preferential allotment of 17 lakh shares.

📍 COLLABORATION

JINDAL STAINLESS: Extends its lubricants and energy-supplies partnership with IOCL for another five years.

RAMCO SYSTEMS: Partners with Altron to expand Ramco Payce payroll solutions across enterprise customers in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

MAPMYINDIA: Partners with MathWorks to accelerate ADAS validation for Indian roads using high-definition maps.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

SRF: Appoints Jyothsana Vasudevan as President & CHRO and Senior Management Personnel effective October 5, 2026.

AXIS BANK: Sanjeev Moghe, Group Head – Branch Banking South, resigns effective October 30, 2026 to pursue an opportunity outside the bank.

MERCURY EV-TECH: Appoints Shreyan Jigneshkumar Patel as Additional Director, Non-Executive Non-Independent, bringing AI/ML and business strategy expertise to the board.

SIEMENS ENERGY: Appoints Ajay Jain as Execution Unit Head – Grid Technologies Transformers, while Ganesh Nadgouda continues as General Manager – Plant Operations.

SUDEEP PHARMA: Managing Director of Sudeep Pharma USA Inc. Sendhil Pani ceases to be Senior Management Personnel effective October 2, 2026.

V-MART RETAIL: President – Merchandising Jayesh Kothari resigns effective October 9, 2026 citing health-related reasons.

ERIS LIFESCIENCES: Executive Director & COO Krishnakumar Vaidyanathan resigns effective September 30, 2026.

KUNDAN MINERALS AND METALS: Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Sonica Verma resigns effective October 15, 2026 to pursue a better career opportunity.

MINDTECK (INDIA): Senior Vice President – Sales Keshava Prasad L resigns for personal reasons, with last working day on October 30, 2026.

PANCHSHEEL ORGANICS: Reappoints Rajesh Abhechand Turakhia as Whole-Time Director, regularises Chandan Mahendra Turakhia as Non-Executive Director and designates Kishor Abhaychand Turakhia as Managing Director.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

RAYMOND REALTY: Plans two premier JDA project launches in MMR with cumulative GDV of over ₹4,100 Cr in H2 FY27 after Q2 pre-sales rose 98% YoY to ₹902 Cr.

BMW INDUSTRIES: Commissions the first phase of its Colour Coating Line at the greenfield downstream steel complex in Bokaro after receiving Consent to Operate.

GRAVITA: Approves incorporation of a wholly owned US subsidiary, Gravita Recyclers USA Inc., with initial capital of USD 50,000 to trade scrap and scrap materials.

OM POWER TRANSMISSION: Incorporates OPTL Green Energy as a 56%-owned subsidiary focused on developing, owning, constructing and operating renewable energy projects.

📍 FUNDRAISING

PIRAMAL FINANCE: Allots 82.94 lakh warrants to promoter group entity Nithyam Realty on preferential basis, with ₹437.51 Cr representing 25% of the total consideration received on allotment.

TRIDENT LIFELINE: Proposes preferential issue of 12.22 lakh equity shares and up to 5.00 lakh warrants at ₹336.60 each, aggregating approximately ₹58 Cr, subject to member approval.

SAFA SYSTEMS & TECHNOLOGIES: Allots 23.90 lakh equity shares to promoters and promoter group on preferential basis at ₹20.47 per share, raising ₹4.89 Cr.

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

PUNJAB & SIND BANK: Fitch assigns BBB- Long-Term IDR with Stable Outlook, reflecting a high probability of extraordinary government support given 94% state ownership.

LIKHITHA INFRASTRUCTURE: CRISIL reaffirms long-term rating at A/Stable and short-term rating at A1 for ₹300 Cr of rated bank facilities.

JSW INFRASTRUCTURE: CARE reaffirms AA+/Stable issuer and long-term facility ratings and A1+ short-term ratings.

UJJIVAN SMALL FINANCE BANK: CRISIL withdraws the A1+ rating on its ₹375 Cr Certificate of Deposits programme at the bank's request.

📍 FII STAKE CHANGES / BOUGHT-SOLD

ROOPA SCREEN: Nine ALPS Opportunity Fund acquires 6.52% stake through IPO allotment and secondary-market purchases.

SHREE SAIBABA EXIM: Acquires an additional 0.352% stake in Evexia Lifecare through open-market purchases, taking its holding to 7.147%.

ICICI PRUDENTIAL MUTUAL FUND: Shareholding in GSPL Transmission exceeds 5% following allotment, with the investment held without controlling intent.

RAJASTHAN GLOBAL SECURITIES: Acquires 9.23% stake in Liqvd Digital India through IPO allotment.

DAMODAR INDUSTRIES: Promoter group member Manju Biyani increases holding to 18.584% through an inter-se transfer of 20 lakh shares.

EMBASSY DEVELOPMENTS: Promoter Jitendra Virwani acquires 3,48,500 shares through the open market.

📍 IPO

RELIANCE INDUSTRIES: Investor feedback on the proposed Jio IPO remains encouraging, with domestic interest reportedly exceeding expectations despite market volatility.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

KOTAK MAHINDRA BANK: Q2 net advances rise 24.7% YoY to ₹5.77 lakh Cr while deposits increase 23.2% YoY to ₹6.51 lakh Cr, with CASA deposits up 11.3% YoY to ₹2.49 lakh Cr.

METROPOLIS HEALTHCARE: Q2 revenue grows approximately 15% YoY on double-digit patient and test-volume growth, while EBITDA margins improve YoY and QoQ.

ACCORD TRANSFORMER & SWITCHGEAR: H1 FY27 revenue rises 90.07% YoY to ₹52.68 Cr, with ₹173 Cr order book and ₹77 Cr of H1 orders received.

PNGS REVA DIAMOND JEWELLERY: Q2 revenue excluding gold sales jumps 46.25% YoY to ₹120.54 Cr, while H1 revenue rises 75.75% YoY to ₹236.53 Cr.

CAPITAL TRUST: Gold-loan disbursements cross ₹45 Cr across 1,800+ customers, while Q2 FY27 AUM rises 25.2% QoQ to approximately ₹300 Cr.

STEEL EXCHANGE INDIA: Records highest-ever monthly and quarterly Re-Bar production, with September output at 25,095 MT and Q2 production at 69,617 MT.

ACCORD TRANSFORMER & SWITCHGEAR: Receives multiple vendor approvals while acquiring 20,300 sq. metres of land in Rajasthan for future expansion.

POPULAR VEHICLES & SERVICES: Step-down subsidiary Zparex Digisolutions commences commercial operations of its automotive spare-parts e-commerce marketplace Yanik.

EMBASSY DEVELOPMENTS: Embassy Origins records over ₹1,800 Cr pre-sales with 477 homes booked and 62% absorption within a week of launch.

ULTRATECH CEMENT: Crosses 2 GW of cumulative green-energy capacity, reaching 2,024 MW and meeting around 48% of current power requirements.

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

RVNL: NSE and BSE imposed fines for non-compliance with SEBI listing regulations relating to board and committee composition, with the company following up with the Ministry of Railways on Independent Director vacancies.

📍 CLARIFICATION

SPICEJET: Clarifies that DGCA's ongoing monitoring of its operational and financial position is routine regulatory oversight and does not indicate a new safety concern.

SRG HOUSING FINANCE: Clarifies that it has received no communication from NHB regarding any forensic audit and confirms there are no defaults in lender repayments.

TATA CHEMICALS: Gujarat court orders no coercive action against Tata Chemicals in the environmental-damage case concerning its marine sanctuary plea.

📍 LAUNCHES

JEENA SIKHO LIFECARE: Launches eight new Ayurvedic and nutraceutical products, including joint-care products and Plant Protein variants for general, men and women categories.

NAZARA TECHNOLOGIES: Subsidiary Fusebox Games launches The Traitors: Interactive Game globally on iOS and Android, expanding its licensed entertainment-IP portfolio.

BHARTI AIRTEL: Launches IQ Gateway, a telco-grade network intelligence platform combining fraud protection, network insights and multi-channel enterprise messaging.

LTM: Launches BlueVerse AgenTraceIQ, an integrated framework for agent observability, governance and resilience across leading enterprise AI ecosystems.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

KPI GREEN ENERGY: Incorporates wholly owned subsidiary KPGC Three Private Limited with ₹1 lakh capital to operate in renewable energy generation, storage and power projects.

LEAP INDIA: Incorporates wholly owned subsidiary Total Integrated Packaging Solutions Private Limited to expand its business operations.

PRISTINE LOGISTICS & INFRAPROJECTS: Amalgamates wholly owned subsidiary Pristine Malwa Logistics Park into the company, resulting in direct holding of 73.41% in Sical Logistics.

AXISCADES: Places German step-down subsidiary add-solution GmbH into voluntary solvent liquidation as part of its exit from automotive engineering services.

EVERVIE HEALTH: Changes its corporate name from PVP Ventures Limited to Evervie Health Limited effective October 5, 2026.

LCC PROJECTS: Board approves incorporation of a new Indian subsidiary.

📍 IT NEWS

COFORGE: Introduces Intent Engineering Framework to help enterprises define, govern and measure AI agents against business outcomes.

MASTEK: Advances its Services as Software strategy with AI-native services combining domain expertise, AI, data and engineering to deliver measurable enterprise outcomes.

TECHD CYBERSECURITY: Receives its largest-ever single purchase order worth ₹13.08 Cr including GST for BFSI deployment of APM, ASM and AIOps platforms.

📍 TAX ORDER

NALCO: Cuts aluminium prices by ₹11,500 per tonne, or 3.2%, amid weaker LME prices and pressure from Chinese exports.

📍 ADDITIONS

SHREE SECURITIES: Proposes reduction of paid-up equity share capital by approximately ₹78.20 Cr to write off accumulated losses and consolidate existing ₹1 shares into ₹10 shares.

ADVANCED ENZYMES: Buys back 30,000 equity shares on October 5, taking cumulative shares bought back to 17.43 lakh.

EMAMI: Buys back 6.50 lakh equity shares on October 5 at an average ₹375.94 per share, taking cumulative buyback to 67.72 lakh shares.

PAISALO DIGITAL: Releases 3.415 Cr pledged shares held by the promoter group following repayment of the related loan.

GAYATRI SUGARS: Releases encumbrance on 59.12 lakh promoter-group shares after debt clearance.

📍 OTHERS

AMBER ENTERPRISES: Fire at subsidiary IL Jin Electronics is estimated to have caused ₹38.28 Cr loss, with insurer releasing a ₹10 Cr advance payment.

ANsal PROPERTIES AND INFRASTRUCTURE: Reports continued loan defaults exceeding 30 days, with ₹94.32 Cr default outstanding and total financial indebtedness of ₹183.37 Cr.

REFEX INDUSTRIES: Promoter holding entity creates additional pledge over 4.13 lakh shares, increasing encumbered shares to 28.71 lakh.

IDEAFORGE: Promoter Ankit Mehta pledges 2.80 lakh shares, representing 0.56% of total share capital, for personal financial requirements.

DISHА RESOURCES: Promoter-group HUF disposes of 4.37% stake through inter-se transfer, reducing its holding to zero.

ORGANIC RECYCLING SYSTEMS: Suhrud C. Patel sells 900 shares through the open market, reducing his holding marginally to 5.26%.

RAVINDRA ENERGY: Promoters pledge a combined 8.57 lakh shares with Tata Capital as security against a company loan.

ANUPAM RASAYAN INDIA: Promoter-group entities create pledges over a combined 1.204 Cr equity shares.

JUST DIAL: Promoter-group inter-se gift transfer increases V.S.S. Mani's holding to 7.89%, with no change in aggregate promoter-group ownership.

AMANTA HEALTHCARE: Promoter-group member transfers 17.33 lakh shares, representing 4.46%, to a nephew by way of gift.

SUDARSHAN CHEMICAL: Transfers 15.89% stake in Sudarshan Colorants from wholly owned subsidiary Sudarshan Europe to the parent, with no change in consolidated promoter holding.

SHRINGAR HOUSE OF MANGALSUTRA: Receives the "Mangalsutra Manufacturer of the Year" award at the India International Jewellery Awards 2026.

VEDANTA: Board to consider the first interim dividend for FY27 on October 8, with October 14 fixed as the record date.

WIPRO: Board to approve Q2 FY27 financial results on October 15 following its October 14–15 meeting.

CYIENT DLM: Board meeting scheduled for October 15 to consider unaudited Q2 FY27 financial results.

LMW: Board meeting scheduled for October 21 to approve unaudited Q2 FY27 financial results.

UTI AMC: Schedules earnings conference call for October 27 to discuss Q2 and H1 FY27 financial performance.

JAYKAY ENTERPRISES: Invests an additional ₹25 Cr in wholly owned subsidiary JK Defence & Aerospace through its rights issue, retaining 100% ownership.

VARDHMAN TEXTILES: Agrees to acquire a minimum 26% stake in Serentica Renewables India 32 for captive renewable power projects.

RELAXO FOOTWEARS: Executes definitive agreements for renewable-energy procurement under the group captive mechanism for its Haryana manufacturing facilities.

BENGAL STEEL / GERMAN STEEL: Majority of sales are generated from Gujarat, with capacity utilisation around 80% and expectations of EBITDA margin rising 4–5% in the near term.

INDIGO: Revises domestic fuel charges to ₹375–₹1,300 based on route distance amid a more than 14% MoM rise in ATF prices.

V2 RETAIL: Reports demand below last year amid inflationary pressures and the onset of festive season, while raw-material prices remain elevated.

SEAMEC: ONGC-owned vessel Samudra Prabha is released from its project for statutory drydocking effective October 5.

TVS MOTORS: Chairman highlights high Chinese imports in batteries and motors and says E10 should not be a mandatory choice for customers.

BHARAT FORGE: Wins a long-term contract for aerospace engine components to be manufactured at its Indian aerospace facility.

BHARAT FORGE / RK FORGINGS / BALAKRISHNA INDUSTRIES: North American Class 8 truck orders decline 10% YoY to 18,700, with Jefferies expecting softer near-term build rates.

MANIPAL PAYMENT: International business grows 2.3x YoY, with management targeting sustained margins and a 30% margin over time.

PANORAMA STUDIOS: Drishyam The Conclusion reaches ₹176.50 Cr India net collection and ₹211.80 Cr domestic gross collection.

KNACK PACKAGING: Expects 30% YoY volume growth and has rented a 43,000 MTPA capacity plant post IPO.

ESAF SFB: Focuses on strengthening MSME relationships and targeting growth in individual savings accounts.

PB FINTECH: Welcomes IRDAI's proposed consultation paper and says at least 70% of its business is expected to remain unaffected.

RUNWAL ENT: Focuses on mid-market and luxury segments, which together are targeted to account for roughly one-third of its portfolio.

BROKING STOCKS: Market-wide MTF book rises 3.6% MoM to ₹1.51 lakh Cr as of September 30, potentially supporting interest income and broking revenues.

WEWORK INDIA: Opens new centres in Bengaluru and Pune, adding approximately 2.25 lakh sq. ft. and more than 4,500 desks.

ULTRATECH CEMENT: Targets an 85% green-energy share by 2030 and 100% by 2050 after crossing 2 GW of captive green-energy capacity.

GAYATRI SUGARS: Promoter encumbrance release follows clearance of the underlying debt.

ARABIAN OIL / ENERGY MARKET: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warns the prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption has triggered the most serious energy supply shock of his career and says rebuilding global stocks could take two years.

NUVAMA / BSE: Securities Appellate Tribunal proceedings continue over the Jane Street case, with portions of the NSE report reportedly redacted by SEBI.

H-ACID | MANUFACTURING COMPLEXITY + INDIA OPPORTUNITY

Value Chain
- Naphthalene → H-Acid.
- H-Acid → Dye intermediates.
- Dye intermediates → Reactive/Acid/Direct dyes.
- Dyes → Textiles, leather, paper and applications.

Why H-Acid Is Difficult
- Conventional route involves multiple chemical stages.
- Naphthalene → Sulphuric acid/Oleum.
- Nitric acid → Reduction.
- Caustic soda → Alkali fusion.
- High-temperature and high-pressure processing required.
- Final stages involve acidification and purification.

Environmental Complexity
- Process generates significant waste.
- Requires serious ETP/ZLD infrastructure.
- Installed capacity may not equal effective capacity.
- Compliant and efficient capacity matters more.

India China+1 Opportunity
- Environmental restrictions can remove inefficient capacity.
- Customers seek reliable non-China suppliers.
- India has established dye-intermediate chemistry.
- Gujarat and Maharashtra have mature ecosystems.
- Indian textiles provide a large downstream market.

Competitive Advantage
- Reliability can matter more than lowest cost.
- Compliant producers may gain pricing power.
- Supply constraints can support sharper pricing.
- Effective capacity is the key industry metric.

Listed H-Acid Exposure
- Shree Hari Chemicals: closest pure-play exposure.
- Bhageria Industries: H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- AksharChem India: H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- AksharChem also has pigments and silica.
- Bodal Chemicals: broad dye-intermediate ecosystem.
- Kiri Industries: integrated H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- Kiri also has dyes and basic chemicals.

Business Model Spectrum
- Pure-play → Higher H-Acid sensitivity.
- Integrated → Diversified chemical exposure.
- Pure-play offers higher H-Acid beta.
- Integrated players offer broader ecosystems.

KEY TAKEAWAY
H-Acid manufacturing is complex, waste-intensive and environmentally demanding. The opportunity may therefore depend more on effective compliant capacity than installed capacity, with reliable Indian producers potentially benefiting from China+1 demand.

The stock trades only once a week (Monday) with a 2% circuit limit.

That’s one reason the valuation can remain at a low PE despite strong fundamentals

INDIAN IT | RUPEE FALL BENEFIT NO LONGER ENOUGH

Old Currency Logic
- IT companies earn significant dollar revenue.
- Profits are reported in Indian rupees.
- Rupee depreciation increases translated revenue.
- Example: $1 Bn becomes more rupees at ₹85/$.
- Currency depreciation historically supported IT earnings.

2026 Disconnect
- Rupee has crossed ₹95/$.
- Nifty IT is down ~29% YTD.
- Traditional currency-benefit relationship has weakened.
- Larger sector challenges are overpowering currency benefits.

Why Currency Benefit Is Limited
- Rupee depreciation can improve reported revenues.
- It cannot create new clients.
- It cannot create additional projects.
- It cannot protect outdated business models.
- AI-related disruption remains a larger concern.

AI Impact
- Traditional IT growth relied heavily on outsourcing.
- Client technology work was delivered through Indian teams.
- AI can automate parts of technology work.
- Fewer engineers may be needed for some projects.
- This could change the traditional hiring-led growth model.

US Market Exposure
- Nearly 57% of sector revenue comes from the US.
- US client spending remains an important demand driver.
- Slower spending can pressure IT growth.
- AI creates additional questions around future pricing.

Sector Weight Decline
- Five largest IT companies now represent ~7.6% of Nifty 50.
- Sector weight exceeded 20% in the early 2000s.
- IT's index influence has therefore declined significantly.

Currency vs Fundamentals
- Rupee depreciation still provides earnings support.
- Currency acts as a cushion for reported earnings.
- Currency cannot solve weak demand.
- Currency cannot eliminate AI-related structural questions.
- Future performance depends on more than exchange rates.

KEY TAKEAWAY
The traditional equation of “weak rupee = positive for IT” is no longer sufficient. Rupee depreciation can support reported earnings, but demand, client spending, AI-driven productivity and pricing dynamics are becoming increasingly important for India's IT sector.

TDPowerSystems has received a new order worth approximately ₹192 crore through its US subsidiary, TDPS USA.

The order is from a leading multinational corporation for the supply of TDPS designed 2 Pole generators used in gas turbine applications. These generators will be installed in the United States, with deliveries scheduled between August 2027 and January 2028.

This is not just another order. The real significance lies in the type of product being supplied.TD Power has won the order using its own in house 2 Pole generator design. Developing and qualifying such generators requires deep engineering expertise, years of experience and customer approvals. Not many companies globally have these capabilities.

Management itself has called this a significant entry into the global 2 Pole generator market.

TD Power is therefore gradually moving up the value chain. Instead of being only a supplier of conventional generators, it is now winning orders in specialized high speed generator applications linked to gas turbines. These are technically demanding products where competition is much lower than in standard industrial generators.

If this project is executed successfully, it can become a strong reference project for future global customers.

When a large multinational corporation places a ₹192 crore order, it is effectively validating TD Power's technology, manufacturing quality and execution capabilities.
Large global customers usually spend months or even years evaluating suppliers before awarding such contracts.

Winning the first large order is often the hardest part. Once proven, repeat orders become easier to secure.

This order also indicates that TD Power is becoming relevant in the global 2 Pole generator market.
The company has previously indicated that the global generator opportunity is significantly larger than the domestic market. Success in this segment could open doors to many more international projects over the next several years.
This is particularly important because exports generally carry better margins and higher profitability compared to many domestic projects.

The order value of ₹192 crore is substantial relative to TD Power's size.
Since deliveries are scheduled between August 2027 and January 2028, this order provides revenue visibility for future periods and strengthens the order book. It also improves confidence in management's plans to increase manufacturing capacity towards ₹3,200 crore revenue capability and eventually beyond ₹4,000 crore.

The ₹192 crore value is important, but the strategic significance may be even bigger than the order size itself.
This order suggests that TD Power is successfully entering a specialized global generator segment where technological barriers are higher and competition is lower. If execution is successful, it could lead to repeat orders, stronger export growth, better margins and a larger share of the global generator market over the coming years.

Cabinet Approval for Four Textile Schemes Likely Soon: Industry Targeted to Reach $350 Billion by 2030 and $2.4 Trillion by 2047

Approval Timeline
The Union Cabinet is expected to approve four key components of the integrated programme for the textile sector announced in the Union Budget in the next two months, Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh said on Thursday

"In one or two months our entire scheme will be approved by the Cabinet," Singh said at a textile conclave organised by Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB), a grassroots organisation representing MSMEs

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the integrated programme for the labour-intensive textile sector in her 2026-27 Budget speech

The programme comprises five sub-components, requiring individual Cabinet approvals for resource allocation and finalisation of operational details

The Schemes
National Fibre Scheme (NFS): will promote self-reliance in natural, man-made and new-age fibres, providing an umbrella framework for existing programmes such as the textile PLI scheme and Kasturi Cotton Bharat

Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme (TEEM): will support modernisation of traditional textile clusters through machinery and technology upgrades and common testing and certification facilities

Tex-Eco: will focus on making Indian textiles and apparel globally competitive and sustainable

Samarth 2.0: will upgrade the sector's skilling ecosystem through greater industry and academic collaboration

Domestic Manufacturing Push
Singh said India would soon begin domestic production of industrial stitching machines, which are currently largely imported

"A Taiwanese company is putting up a facility near Coimbatore which will start production soon," he said, signalling an effort to deepen domestic manufacturing capabilities in textile machinery

Credit Availability
The textiles ministry also held discussions with the Department of Financial Services to improve credit availability for the sector

"After the meetings credit flow to the units in the sector has started to improve gradually," he said

Long-Term Targets (Viksit Bharat 2047)
Industry size: from around $190 billion currently to $350 billion by 2030 and $2.4 trillion by 2047

Textile exports: from around $40 billion currently to $100 billion by 2030 and $600 billion by 2047

Core Theme
The government expects Cabinet approval within one to two months for the key components of its Budget-announced integrated textile programme, covering fibre self-reliance (NFS), cluster modernisation (TEEM), global competitiveness and sustainability (Tex-Eco) and skilling (Samarth 2.0), alongside efforts to produce stitching machines domestically and ease credit, as part of a roadmap to lift the industry from about $190 billion to $350 billion by 2030 and exports from $40 billion to $100 billion.

Adani Green Expands Battery Storage Limit: Operational BESS Capacity Reaches 6.63 GWh, Over Half of India's Total; Firm Aims for 50 GWh in Five Years

The Milestone
Adani Green Energy (AGEL) has expanded its operational battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity to 6.63 GWh, taking its share to more than half of India's operational BESS capacity of about 12.6 GWh

The capacity has nearly doubled from 3.55 GWh in June 2026

AGEL has achieved almost 70% of its FY27 target of adding over 10 GWh of battery storage capacity

The milestone was reached within 14 months of commencing on-site BESS construction at Khavda, and the latest addition was commissioned within 10 months of construction starting

What the Capacity Can Do
The 6.63 GWh BESS at Khavda, Gujarat, can store enough clean electricity to power around two million homes a day

It can support the peak electricity demand of cities such as Nagpur, Patna or Vizag for several hours

The company said the Khavda installation is the world's largest operational battery energy storage system at a single location

Integration and Technology
The facility is integrated with AGEL's renewable energy development at Khavda, where it is developing a 30 GW renewable energy plant across 538 sq km of barren land

The BESS uses lithium-ion battery technology, integrated with energy management systems and automated telemetry to manage charging and discharging, optimise system performance and support grid services

Battery storage helps manage peak demand, improve grid stability and reduce renewable energy curtailment

Future Plans
AGEL is targeting 50 GWh of storage capacity over the next five years and is also pursuing pumped-storage projects as part of its plan to build firm and dispatchable renewable power capacity

Sagar Adani, executive director, Adani Green Energy: "Reaching 6.63 GWh of operational battery storage in just 14 months is a significant milestone for AGEL and India's clean energy transition"

"At this scale, storage can make renewable power firmer, more reliable and dispatchable when the grid needs it"

"As India's power demand grows, we will continue to scale energy storage solutions, both battery and pumped storage, to support a more resilient, lower-carbon grid"

Core Theme
Adani Green has nearly doubled its operational battery storage to 6.63 GWh at Khavda, the world's largest single-location BESS and over half of India's total, reaching almost 70% of its FY27 target of adding 10 GWh in record construction time, as it pursues a 50 GWh goal over five years, backed by battery and pumped-storage projects, to make its renewable power firmer, more dispatchable and grid-ready.

UPI Continues to Grow Strongly, Volumes Up 23%: 24.07 Billion Transactions Worth ₹29.37 Trillion in September 2026

Year-on-Year Growth
UPI volumes grew 22.6% YoY to 24.07 billion in September 2026, from 19.63 billion in September 2025

Value of transactions grew 18% to ₹29.37 trillion, from ₹24.89 trillion in September 2025

Month-on-Month Dip
UPI volumes declined 1.8% from 24.51 billion in August, partly because September had 30 days compared with 31 days in August

Transaction value fell 1.5% to ₹29.37 trillion from ₹29.82 trillion in the previous month

The dip is not unusual: 10 of the past 24 months (including September) saw a low single-digit (1.0 to 2.3%) MoM decline in volumes due to fewer days

On three instances, the decline was between 5.2% and 6.7%; two were in February (2025 and 2026), which have 2-3 days fewer than January, and one was in November 2024, attributed to Diwali being in October 2024

The last 30-day month, June, saw 22.72 billion transactions worth ₹28.92 trillion

Daily Averages
UPI clocked its highest average daily transaction volume of 802 million payments in September

Average daily value of all transactions was ₹97,913 crore in the same month

In June, daily transactions were 757 million, with a value of ₹96,405 crore

Festive Season and MDR
Reeju Datta, cofounder of Cashfree: "This rise came from the start of the festive season. Ganesh Chaturthi fell in mid-September this year, and people began spending on festivities"

From April to August, the money moving through UPI each day had stayed at around ₹96,000 crore even as payments grew, because most new payments were small

Trade groups had previously raised concerns over the introduction of the merchant discount rate (MDR), ending six years of zero-charge UPI transactions

Effective October 15, the NPCI will introduce an MDR structure for select UPI payments

Core Theme
UPI continued its strong run in September 2026, with volumes up 22.6% to 24.07 billion and value up 18% to ₹29.37 trillion YoY and record daily volumes of 802 million payments on the back of early festive spending, while the small MoM dip is a calendar effect, with the bigger change ahead as NPCI introduces an MDR structure on select UPI payments from October 15, ending six years of zero-charge transactions.

Anup Saha Is New Kotak Bank MD & CEO: Three-Year Term Begins January 1, 2027, Ending Leadership Uncertainty

The Appointment
Kotak Mahindra Bank Whole-time Director Anup Saha will be managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) of the lender for a term of three years

The bank said on Thursday that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had given its nod to the appointment, effective January 1, 2027

Saha, 56, is executive director overseeing retail banking, data analytics and marketing

The approval ends the leadership uncertainty at the bank since incumbent MD & CEO Ashok Vaswani announced his exit in June

In June, the bank had said Vaswani would not seek reappointment due to personal reasons when his term ended in December; he assumed office on January 1, 2024, for a three-year term

Saha joined the bank in January this year

He could serve until he turns 70, subject to approval by the board and RBI, providing a longer leadership horizon for strategic and operational changes

Saha's Statement
"I look forward to working with my colleagues to deepen customer relationships, tirelessly execute and build sustainable value for shareholders and all our stakeholders"

"We will remain firmly focused on doing the right thing and getting it right by the customer"

Analyst Views
Citi: the decision delivers strategic continuity while installing a retail/consumer banking-focused leader at the helm; constructive on two counts, reaccelerating growth and easing the overhang of capital deployment

Other brokerages see Saha's key priorities as stabilising the organisation and stemming senior-level exits, accelerating balance-sheet growth to improve return on equity (RoE), building a more granular liabilities franchise, and improving turnaround time and responsiveness across the bank

Suresh Ganapathy, MD & head of India research, Macquarie Capital: "The single-biggest priority is to drive loan growth and deposit growth." Kotak's RoE is the lowest among its large peers, and the only way to improve it is to consume more capital and drive up leverage through faster balance-sheet growth

Another priority is making the deposit base granular, as deposits above ₹5 crore formed almost 23% of the balance sheet as of June 2025, and he would look to see this proportion coming down

Jefferies: Saha has experience leading the retail segment at Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank; timely team reorganisation, if any, will help; "an uptick in the bank's retail deposit and net interest income (NII) growth, along with operational efficiencies, can lift earnings"

Saha's Background
Over 32 years' professional experience, including 25 years in financial services across banking and non-banking financial institutions

Associated with Bajaj Finance, the largest private sector NBFC, from 2017: roles from president (consumer finance), followed by deputy CEO (consumer; MSMEs; marketing; operations and service; digital platform), executive director, deputy MD, and finally MD & CEO from April 2025 until his resignation in July the same year

14 years at ICICI Bank, as senior general manager and group product head overseeing retail home loans, vehicle loans, developer funding and the credit-card business

GE Capital from 1999 to 2003 (credit cards, sales and analytics) and Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd from 1991 to 1995 (production engineering, then a brief stint in sales of consumer durables)

Alumnus of IIT Kharagpur and IIM Lucknow

Core Theme
Kotak Mahindra Bank has named Anup Saha, a retail-focused executive with experience at Bajaj Finance, ICICI Bank and GE Capital, as MD & CEO for a three-year term starting January 1, 2027, ending the leadership uncertainty since Ashok Vaswani's exit announcement. Analysts expect strategic continuity with a push on loan and deposit growth, a more granular liabilities franchise, stabilising the senior team and lifting the bank's return on equity, currently the lowest among large peers.

INDIA CNC MACHINING | SKILLED WORKFORCE + DEFENCE EXPORT OPPORTUNITY

CNC Adoption
- India continues importing more CNC machines.
- Machine availability is not the main constraint.
- Skilled operators remain critical for utilization.
- CNC adoption among small factories grew 18% in 2025.
- Switching costs are gradually declining.

Skilled Workforce Gap
- Aerospace and defence parts require precision machining.
- Every order can involve different specifications.
- Machinists select tools and adjust machine settings.
- Operators must monitor tool wear closely.
- Machines repeat programmed instructions.
- India trains ~68,000 machinists annually through ITIs.
- Source highlights a significant workforce requirement gap.

Small Factory Opportunity
- India has ~72 Mn small and medium factories.
- Rajkot and Ludhiana retain significant manual machining.
- Around 60–65% reportedly still use manual machines.
- CNC upgrades can improve manufacturing precision.
- Delayed adoption can affect competitiveness.

Government Support
- Government support can offset CNC transition costs.
- Factories may receive 4–6% of additional sales.
- Banks can finance up to 85% of machine costs.
- Small businesses can therefore access equipment financing.

Aerospace & Defence Demand
- European defence spending is increasing sharply.
- Europe remains dependent on defence imports.
- Aerospace and missile components require precision machining.
- European manufacturers need additional production capacity.
- Indian suppliers are receiving defence component orders.

India Defence Exports
- India's defence exports reached ₹21,000 Cr last year.
- Government targets ₹50,000 Cr by FY29.
- European defence demand creates export opportunities.
- Indian manufacturers are entering global supply chains.
- CNC machining remains critical for precision components.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India's CNC opportunity extends beyond machine sales. Skilled machinists, factory upgrades and precision manufacturing capacity are becoming increasingly important as aerospace and defence exports expand. The combination of CNC adoption and global defence demand could support India's precision-component manufacturing ecosystem.

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Jury is still out. Ultravolt looks prepared. Space will remain interesting

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.

Impact of change in EV subsidy policy from 31 July 2026

PM E-DRIVE subsidy for electric 2Ws ended on 31 Jul 2026. Govt earlier plan was to support E2W till 31 Mar 2026, then gave the industry a 4-month extension till Jul-end as there was unutilized budget

PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in Oct'24 with a 10,900 Cr outlay. The idea was simple: help EV adoption scale while supporting charging infra, buses, trucks & other EV segments

initially, e-2W buyers got subsidy of 5,000/kWh, capped at 10,000/ vehicle. That was a meaningful discount for mass-market scooters. From Apr'25, cut by half to 2,500/kWh with max capped at 5,000/Veh. Signalling gradual withdrawal of support.

Now for 2W, even that 5,000 support is gone. Effective acquisition cost of an EV scooter will move up. 5,000 price hike may not sound huge, but in entry-level its imp for price-sensitive consumer

Some moderation in electric 2W demand was expected. OEMs were preparing for it as subsidy-led growth gradually transitions to product-led growth. 

August EV 2W market share came lower than July. E2W MS has come down but not in 3w as July subsidy withdrawal only 2W not in 3W. August is typically a non-festival month & seasonality also matters. OEMs should absorb subsidy via better exchange / financing offers

Market is also looking for next phase of EV support. Discussions around "FAME III" continue, but indications suggest focus could shift towards vehicle other than 2W. 2W penetration already >10% while other segment need more support

If electric 2Ws are eventually excluded from future demand subsidies, industry economics will increasingly depend on product quality, distribution, service network & battery costs instead of govt incentives.

One factor often ignored: OEMs capacity are planned in a way where capacity expansion will happen in same facility. Hence, incremental capex intensity will be far lower. Gradual drivetrain shift will continue without large incremental capex

Bottom line: Subsidy withdrawal may create short-term demand noise, but the long-term story remains the same. India's 2W market is enormous, EV penetration is still low, and the migration from ICE to EV is likely to be a long, gradual journey rather than a subsidy-driven sprint.
